inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built: 10-year G-sec ~6.6% + beta 0.7 (large-cap Indian pharma, defensive) x India equity risk premium ~6.5% = cost of equity ~11.1%. Standalone Sun is net cash, so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 11.0%. Equivalent to roughly 8.5% in USD after a ~2.5pp inflation differential. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not the rate. Terminal growth 5.0% INR nominal (about 2.5% USD-equivalent; two-thirds of sales are foreign-currency).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities of 5,478.0m are inside total_debt; lease principal (FY2026 1,513.7m) is NOT deducted from the flows; EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116. Right-of-use renewal (~0.3% of revenue) is carried inside the capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial after the FY2025 Taro buy-out (book 2,838.5m; profit share ~290m a year). Deducted once, in the bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route) with the non-US adaptations. Sun is an operating pharmaceutical company (branded generics, US generics, Innovative Medicines, API), not a financial, trust or holdco, so the routing table's operating-company row applies; no prior valuation exists for this ticker. | ORGANON: Sun signed on 27-Apr-2026 to buy Organon & Co. for USD 14.00/share cash, enterprise value USD 11.75bn, roughly Sun's own revenue again; Organon shareholders approved 23-Jul-2026, most regulatory approvals are in, close expected early 2027. It has NOT closed and Organon's financials are not in this folder, so this is a STANDALONE Sun valuation on Sun's pre-deal balance sheet. The deal is treated as NPV-neutral in the base case (about 6x EBITDA for a flat-to-declining portfolio is roughly fair at an 11% rate; that view rests on general knowledge of Organon, not on filings read here). Its risk is carried in the scenario weights. REBUILD ON CLOSE as a pro-forma: base revenue, margin, D&A and net debt all change, and about USD 11.75bn of the cash pile and new borrowings is spent. | EBITDA is the company's definition, excluding other income (FY2026 177,314m = 30.3% of revenue). Other income (19,717m in FY2026: interest, dividends, fair-value and FX gains) is excluded from the flows; the assets that earn it are in net cash and the bridge. | Exceptional items (FY2026 13,075m; H1 FY2027 14,729m: Organon deal costs 5,132m, antitrust settlement 9,227m, labour-code 371m) are outside EBITDA. The 9,226.7m antitrust settlement signed 10-Sep-2026 is assumed unpaid at 30-Sep (provisions rose 10.6bn in the half) and is deducted net of its tax benefit in the bridge. | Capex is PP&E plus intangibles as reported; acquisitions of subsidiaries (FY2026 34,051m Checkpoint; H1 FY2027 2,877m Innovcare) are not in capex, so the growth path is meant as organic plus in-licensing only. | Working capital is a real drag: receivables + inventory less payables is about 36% of revenue, so wc_capture is negative. | Price is a regular-session print, not after-hours.

equity_bridge.note: 30-Sep-2026 balance sheet; mostly fair-valued. Their dividend and fair-value income is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule). Includes the pre-deal Organon stake (12.5m shares, 7,064.8m at 31-Mar-2026).

equity_bridge.item: US generic-pricing antitrust settlement signed 10-Sep-2026, net of tax benefit
equity_bridge.note: 9,226.7m less 953.4m tax credit (Q2 FY2027 results note 4c). Assumed provided but unpaid at 30-Sep-2026.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5-year CAGR (31.6%) diverges from equity CAGR (12.5%) by more than 30%: the FY2021 base (EPS 12.1) was depressed by 43bn of exceptional items. Revenue (11.8%) and owner FCF (12.0%) agree with equity. FCF 3-year CAGR (45.3%) is off a working-capital-depressed FY2023 base and is not a signal.
historical_growth.notes: FY2021/FY2023 -> FY2026. Owner FCF equals reported FCF throughout: SBC is nil and interest income is already outside operating cash flow in the Ind AS format, so the series is consistent without adjustment. Reported FCF: FY2021 50,002; FY2023 28,738; FY2024 99,332; FY2025 119,435; FY2026 88,098. FY2025 was flattered by a 3.5% cash tax rate, FY2026 held back by a 36bn capex year. Trailing twelve months to Sep-2026 is about 77.7bn (H1 is seasonally weak on receivables, and cash tax tripled year on year). The base path starts growth below the 12.5% equity CAGR, at the 10-11% the revenue line is actually delivering.

base.growth_note: Year 1 is FY2027: H1 revenue was +11.2% (India +16.6%, EM +6%, RoW +1.5% in USD, US -8% in USD on generic erosion, INR depreciation helping); H2 laps a strong Q3 FY2026.
base.margin_note: FY2026 30.3%, H1 FY2027 29.1% (launch spend on Leqselvi/Unloxcyt, loss of high-margin US generic contribution). Recovers to 30.5% as Innovative Medicines scale.
base.tax_note: Cash tax was 15.3% of PBT in FY2026 and 18% in H1 FY2027 on MAT-credit use; the book rate has stepped up to about 28% pre-exceptional in H1 FY2027 as the parent moved to the 25.17% section 115BAA regime. Ramped to a 25% blended normal rate by year 3.

scenario_narratives.base: India branded formulations (a third of sales, No.1 with 8.6% share and gaining) keep compounding at low double digits on new launches and field-force reach; Innovative Medicines (about 21% of sales: Ilumya incl. the new psoriatic-arthritis label, Winlevi, Cequa, Leqselvi, Unloxcyt) grow around 10% a year in USD; US generics keep eroding mid-single digits with Halol still under import alert; emerging markets and RoW grow mid-to-high single digits helped by INR depreciation. Revenue growth fades from 10% to 5.5% over ten years. EBITDA margin dips to 29% on launch spend, then recovers to 30.5% as specialty scales. Cash tax normalises to 25% as MAT credits run off. Organon closes and earns about what was paid for it.
scenario_narratives.bull: The specialty pivot works at scale: Ilumya's psoriatic-arthritis label, Leqselvi and Unloxcyt each become meaningful, Innovative Medicines pass 30% of sales and lift the margin to 33%; India adds GLP-1 (semaglutide) to an already share-gaining franchise; Halol is cleared and the 120 pending ANDAs start to offset generic erosion; the PCSK9 licence opens cardiovascular outside the US. Organon is bought well and its biosimilars and women's-health reach add value beyond the purchase price (not in the flows here, so this case understates that outcome). Growth holds at 11-12% for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The US turns hostile on both sides of the book: generic price erosion and tariff or most-favoured-nation pricing pressure hit generics and specialty alike, further FDA action widens beyond Halol to Mohali or Dadra, and the new launches stall against entrenched IL-23 and JAK competitors. NPPA price caps tighten on the India portfolio. More generic-pricing antitrust settlements follow the two already taken. Growth falls to 5% and the margin slides to 26% as specialty spend fails to earn out. Organon turns out to be a levered purchase of a shrinking franchise (Nexplanon loss of exclusivity, established-brands decay), consuming the cash pile for less than it cost.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% rather than the 15% default: Sun is about to spend USD 11.75bn, the whole net cash pile plus new debt, on a levered acquisition as large as itself by revenue, with a history of FDA compliance lapses and a single regulator (US FDA) gating the specialty and generic pipeline. Base 50%: the India franchise and the existing specialty book are proven and the first-half numbers are tracking this path. Bull 25% rather than 35%: it needs several independent things to go right at once: three recent launches scaling, Halol clearance, and a clean Organon integration.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Standalone owner-FCF value of Sun at an INR-built 11% rate, with the cash pile counted once at face and the pending Organon deal treated as value-neutral. On that basis the market price is well above every scenario: at about 23x trailing EBITDA and 37x adjusted earnings the price is paying for a discount rate near 9% together with terminal growth near 6%, or for a specialty outcome better than the bull case. The quality of the India franchise is not in doubt; the price is.
key_risks_to_valuation: Organon is not in the model. On close the balance sheet flips from about 300bn net cash to roughly 2.3x net debt/EBITDA and revenue nearly doubles; if the deal earns well above or below its cost, this valuation is wrong by that amount.
Discount rate: Indian large-cap pharma trades on an implied rate well under 11%. The required-return table shows what the price implies.
Cash tax: the path assumes 25% by year 3. A slower run-off of MAT credits helps the early years; a higher US or global minimum-tax burden hurts all of them.
Working capital at 36% of revenue makes free cash flow sensitive to growth and to US channel terms; H1 FY2027 absorbed 34bn.
Reported in INR with two-thirds of sales abroad: sustained INR depreciation flatters growth and is partly what the 5% terminal growth rate relies on.
The antitrust settlement is assumed unpaid at 30-Sep-2026; if it was already paid, value is about 3.4 per share higher. Further claims are possible.
